title: 3M Reaches Broad Resolution of AFFF Personal Injury Litigation
summary: 3M to make $5.8 billion present value commitment through 2034 to resolve MDL personal injury claims, substantially reducing litigation risk and uncertainty SAINT PAUL, Minn., Nov. 3, 2026...
body_markdown:
*3M to make $5.8 billion present value commitment through 2034 to resolve MDL personal injury claims, substantially reducing litigation risk and uncertainty*


SAINT PAUL, Minn.


, Nov. 3, 2026


/[PRNewswire](http://www.prnewswire.com/) / -- 3M (NYSE: MMM) has entered into a broad resolution to settle PFAS-related personal injury claims that are the focus of the Aqueous Film-Forming Foam Multi-District Litigation ("AFFF MDL") in federal district court in South Carolina. The resolution also positions 3M to manage remaining and future personal injury claims both inside and outside the AFFF MDL.


Under the agreement, 3M will make a pre-tax $7.35 billion nominal commitment over nine years, with a present value of $5.8 billion. The agreement:


- Addresses approximately 99% of current personal injury claims inside and outside the AFFF MDL, involving approximately 115,000–120,000 plaintiffs eligible to participate in the resolution, including all personal injury claims that have been the focus of the AFFF MDL litigation.
- Includes a $50 million payment in 2026, and no payments in 2027, with approximately 20% of payments due in the final two years, to align to 3M's remaining payment obligations for other legacy settlements.


Remaining and future personal injury claims, both inside and outside the AFFF MDL, will be managed through several settlement mechanisms. These include payments contingent on plaintiffs joining the resolution, a $680 million reserve fund included in the overall financial commitment, and an anticipated MDL court order establishing evidentiary and timing requirements for plaintiffs who may seek to litigate in the future.


"This settlement is a significant milestone for 3M and substantially reduces litigation uncertainty," said William Brown, 3M Chairman and CEO. "Following our 2023 resolution with U.S. public water suppliers and our more recent settlement with the State of New Jersey, this is another important step in managing legacy PFAS matters. With this, we will continue our focus on transforming the enterprise, strengthening operating rigor and delivering predictable, long-term performance."


The legacy claims settled today primarily relate to PFAS compounds that 3M announced in 2000 it would voluntarily phase out and did so. In 2022, 3M further announced it would discontinue the manufacture of all PFAS globally by the end of 2025, and 3M successfully met that goal. 3M has invested in state-of-the-art water treatment technologies at sites where it historically manufactured PFAS and 3M will continue to remediate PFAS at those sites.


This agreement is not an admission of liability. If certain agreed settlement terms are not fulfilled, 3M is prepared to continue to defend itself in litigation.


**Financial Considerations**
As a result of the settlement, the company will record a pre-tax charge of $5.8 billion in the fourth quarter of 2026, representing the present value of contributions under the agreement. This charge will be reflected as a special item when arriving at 3M's adjusted results, and does not change 3M's previously issued 2026 guidance. The payment structure, over nine years, provides predictable cash flow with payments aligned to reflect other company obligations. Additional details will be included in 3M's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.


The strength and stability of 3M's business model and strong free cash flow capability, together with proven capital markets access, provide financial flexibility to meet its cash flow needs under this agreement and other obligations, as well as to fund other investment and growth priorities.
